title: Get ready for 3 consecutive rate hikes starting next month, bank economist warns
excerpt: "We believe the FOMC, in its three upcoming meetings, will remove three more doses of accommodation," Egelhof wrote.
content_html:
By William Edwards

A hat trick of Federal Reserve rate hikes is on the way, BNP Paribas says.

In a note published late last week, BNP Paribas chief US economist James Egelhof said he sees three 25-basis-point hikes coming in quick succession at the Fed's December, January, and March meetings.

That would put the fed funds rate at 4.5%-4.75%, up from its 3.75%-4% range.

"We believe the FOMC, in its three upcoming meetings, will remove three more doses of accommodation," Egelhof wrote.

"We have added this additional hike because we believe the economy is showing a high level of resilience to firmer interest rates, suggesting that the short-run neutral interest rate is higher than expected," he added.

According to the CME's FedWatch tool, markets are pricing in 95% odds of a hike at the Fed's December meeting, and 59% odds of another hike at its January meeting. Market consensus is not yet behind a March hike, however, with odds at 31%.

BNP said the economy has not cooled sufficiently following the Fed's September rate hike and that further tightening is needed. It cited strong jobs reports and sticky inflation.

Indeed, the US economy added 186,000 jobs in August and 165,000 jobs in October. The consumer price index has also stayed well above 3% year-over-year in 2026, though there was no year-over-year reading in October. The Fed's stated long-term target on inflation is 2%.

Non-shelter services inflation in particular has been hot, showing that inflationary trends are going beyond geopolitical shocks like elevated oil prices, the bank said.

Despite BNP's view that the Fed will be more aggressive than investors expect over the next few meetings, the bank doesn't see Fed chair Warsh and the Federal Open Market Committee going overboard with hikes.

In other words, the central bank is going to take a middle-of-the-road sort of stance. While it will tighten policy to help fight inflation, it will actively try to avoid throwing the economy into recession by setting rates too high, BNP said. A 4.5%-4.75% range is its sweet spot.

"Hiking much beyond this level could result in a restrictive monetary policy stance, leading to job losses and slower growth," Egelhof wrote. "To date, the FOMC has shown no interest in such a policy."

However, while the labor market could prove durable enough to withstand a few hikes, AI stocks could suffer from such an outcome, BNP said.

The AI trade has already suffered steep declines in recent weeks, with the Nasdaq 100 approaching bear-market territory.

"A concerning scenario for our forecast would be a lasting reappraisal among investors about the wisdom of investing in AI-related businesses or facilities," Egelhof said.
